name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Federation no longer uses real Jellyfin API keys between friends. Previously, connecting two servers minted each side a genuine Jellyfin API key - and in Jellyfin, any valid API key is full-admin-equivalent, satisfying the same authorization check as this server's own admin session. That meant every friend you ever added held a key capable of anything on your server: creating/deleting users, deleting libraries, installing plugins - not just federation. Friends now exchange a custom, opaque federation token instead, generated and checked entirely by this plugin, never registered with Jellyfin's own authentication system - it satisfies nothing outside federation's own endpoints, full stop.

This required moving every friend-to-friend data call off Jellyfin's native REST API (which only ever accepts real Jellyfin credentials) onto new endpoints this plugin owns and enforces itself: Peer/Libraries, Peer/Items, Peer/PlaybackInfo, Peer/Users, Peer/SystemInfo, plus token-gated gateways for streaming (already existed) and now images too (previously hotlinked a friend's native image API, optionally with a raw api_key query param - now token-gated the same way video already was). Every one of these applies your sharing scope and per-user rules in this plugin's own code before returning anything - which finally makes "restrict this friend to certain libraries" and "restrict one of their specific users" work without a Jellyfin account in the loop at all: the old model required creating a dedicated, hidden local Jellyfin user just to enforce a restriction via Jellyfin's native permission system, which is now gone entirely. Restricting a friend is just picking libraries (or specific items - new per-friend exclude list) directly.

Also added, while rebuilding this: per-remote-user restriction is now enforced at the actual moment playback is granted (previously only checked earlier, at browse/sync time, which a stale cached rule or a bookmarked URL could outlive), and removing a friend now notifies them and revokes their token immediately, instead of requiring both sides to separately click unfriend.

This is a hard, deliberate protocol break: a server on this version cannot federate with a friend still on an older one - both sides need to upgrade. Sending or accepting a friend request with an incompatible version now fails with a clear message instead of silently misbehaving.

210 tests (up from 200).
